Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints consistent with cervical
whiplash injury. The reported mechanism of injury fits well with the kind and force of the impact. Over the course of
care, the patient attended 30 visits, including physical therapy, manual therapy, and home exercise instruction.
Treatment followed a typical progression and tapered as symptoms improved, with reduced neck stiffness, improved
range of motion, and fewer headaches reported in later visits. Cervical imaging and physical examination findings
clearly confirm the soft tisuse injury. The patient was also treated for the same region within the past two years, and
that prior condition contributes to some of the current symptoms, which has been considered in the plan of care.
Billing records show two similar charges on the same date of service, which are currently under review for accuracy.
